segments.narration: Nobody buys silver at spot. Here is what the markup really pays for, and when it is too much.

A 1 oz American Silver Eagle typically runs about 20 percent over spot. Spot at 32 dollars means roughly 38 dollars and 40 cents at checkout. That gap is the premium. It covers minting, dealer overhead, insured shipping, and profit.
segments.explanation: A 1 oz American Silver Eagle typically costs 18 to 25 percent over spot at online dealers

segments.text: THE PREMIUM MOVES ON ITS OWN
segments.narration: The premium does not follow the chart. It follows physical demand. When buyers rush in faster than mints can produce, premiums climb even while spot falls. Two purchases at the same spot price can cost very different amounts weeks apart.
segments.explanation: Premiums follow physical demand, not the chart

segments.narration: Bars are the cheap way to buy ounces. A 10 oz bar runs 4 to 6 percent over spot. Generic 1 oz rounds run 5 to 8. Government coins like Eagles run about 20. Same silver. The difference is minting cost and brand recognition.
segments.explanation: A 10 oz bar runs 4 to 6 percent over spot while a government coin runs about 20 percent

segments.narration: Small coins flip the math completely. A one tenth ounce coin can run 130 percent over spot. The 1 oz version of the same coin runs about 12. The smaller the product, the bigger the premium per ounce.
segments.explanation: A 1/10 oz coin can cost 130 percent over spot versus about 12 percent for the 1 oz version

segments.title: Typical Premium Over Spot by Product
segments.narration: This is the whole premium picture in one chart. Eagles run about 20 percent over spot. Generic rounds about 7. Ten ounce bars about 5. If your goal is the most ounces for your money, bars win. If you want recognizability when you sell, Eagles earn part of that premium back.

Most dealers list two prices. Card and PayPal orders cost about 4 percent more than check, wire, or eCheck. On a 1,000 dollar order that is 40 dollars for the convenience of plastic. Shipping works the same way. Small orders carry the cost badly.
segments.explanation: Card and PayPal orders cost about 4 percent more than check or wire at most dealers

segments.text: YOU DON'T GET THE PREMIUM BACK
segments.narration: Here is the part nobody tells beginners. When you sell, dealers pay near spot, sometimes 1 to 3 percent under it. You do not get the premium back. A 20 percent premium going in means spot has to rise about 20 percent before you break even.
segments.explanation: Dealers buy back near spot, sometimes 1 to 3 percent under it

segments.narration: Run this check on every quote. Take the all-in total including shipping. Divide by the troy ounces. Subtract spot, then divide by spot. A 38 dollar 40 cent coin at 32 dollar spot is 20 percent. Ten seconds, and you know exactly what you are paying for.
segments.explanation: Total paid divided by ounces, minus spot, divided by spot
